text: ConsciousnessEngine (used by anima_unified.py) — OWNER DECISION on two measured defects. (1) cell_tension = 0.5 is assigned to the FIRST cell of every step's loop, sits above split_threshold=0.3, and is the sole cause of all 148 splits in a 300-step run; computed tension peaks at 0.037 and never reaches the bar. Removing the constant stops division entirely, as it did in MitosisEngine. (2) The computed branch measures deviation from the mean of cells processed SO FAR, not the population, so tension falls with loop position (0.024 at cell 1, 0.007 at cell 4) — the same cell in a different position gets a different value. Making it population-wide changes what tension means. Measured in docs/tension-is-not-one-quantity.md; annotated at the site, not changed.

EmpathyEthics (trinity.py) cannot refuse — OWNER DECISION. allowed = phi_preservation > 0.3, and phi_preservation takes exactly two values (0.5 warning, 1.0 ok), both above the bar, so allowed is True in every situation including Phi collapsing 10->0 with pain at maximum. Two more dead paths in the same class: empathy_threshold=0.3 is stored by __init__ and never read anywhere; and no caller reads allowed (trinity.py:1401 takes empathy/reciprocity/phi_preservation and drops the verdict). The E module of the Hexad is structurally incapable of refusing and unconsulted; NoEthics right below it is the same behaviour under an honest name. Deciding what should block is a design decision. Measured in docs/fake-measurement-audit.md, annotated at the site. Also flagged there: autonomous_loop.py:460 novelty = 0.5 sits in a bare except and needs a runtime check.

MitosisEngine split axis — OWNER DECISION on landing bench_specialization_split.py (3ee08d4). Measured: aggregating tension per STIMULUS instead of per consecutive STEP is the only design this session that settles between floor and ceiling under varying input (9.0-14.0 cells from a 2-cell start), holds within 1.24x when the ceiling moves 16->64, and cuts scale drift 967%->79%. The step axis cannot work: split_patience needs consecutive steps above the bar, but with rotating stimuli the loudest cell rotates too, so 4/8/16-cell starts froze at exactly their starting size. NOT landed in the engine -- 3 seeds on synthetic vectors refutes a design but does not justify changing how a running engine divides; needs real corpus stimuli first. Also flagged at mitosis.py:12 -- H297 ('N=2 optimal start') is cited in 4 places with no hypothesis document anywhere; the backed claim is CB1, 'min 2 differentiated cells for Phi>1', a floor for existence and not an operating point. min_cells=2 stands; initial_cells is a separate unsettled choice.

merge_threshold = 0.05 is the seventh instance of the root defect, and the one that actually governs population on real data (42ad42f). Measured over 400 steps at 16 cells: inter-cell tension on real corpus sentences has median 0.0148 and p90 0.0205, so it sits below the 0.05 bar 100.0% of the time -- the bar is 2.4x above the 90th percentile of what real language produces. On synthetic randn vectors the same tension has median 0.0830 and falls below only 9.3%. Consequence: real corpus gives 7 splits against 21 merges and collapses 16 cells -> 2 at every bar and every starting size, while synthetic gives 8 splits against 6 merges and holds 18. Split rates barely differ; the merge side decides everything. This kills the per-stimulus split design from #3 -- it does not survive its own corpus gate, and its synthetic success was an artifact of near-orthogonal stimuli (corpus sentences under text_vector have mean pairwise cosine +0.191 vs randn +0.014, 14x closer). OWNER DECISION: the merge bar and the split bar are one decision and must be settled together; annotated at mitosis.py _check_merges, not changed. Method note: synthetic stimuli made a broken configuration look regulated across three independent properties, so any future population mechanism gets measured on corpus text before it is believed.

Inter-cell tension does not carry stimulus-diversity information -- this closes the population-regulation arc (#3, #4). Measured on NARROW (24 corpus sentences, internal cosine +0.435) vs BROAD (+0.037), same pool: raw inter-cell tension median 0.01083 vs 0.01070 (0.99x), p10 identical at 0.00421. Internal similarity differs 12-fold; the quantity does not move. Therefore NO threshold on it -- absolute, calibrated, rank, quantile or z-score -- can regulate population against input diversity. Making both sides relative (split = top decile of cells, merge = bottom decile of pairs) collapses to the floor 2.0 at every quantile pair on every stimulus set, because a rank puts the bottom at exactly 0.00 and the top at exactly 1.00 by construction, so both rules fire unconditionally and merges (13.3) beat splits (7.3). A z-score was measured before being built: median min-z -1.90 narrow vs -1.62 broad with an IDENTICAL 33.3% below -2, so it would not distinguish either. OWNER DECISION now upstream of #3/#4: any population regulation needs a signal that responds to stimulus-set diversity, and inter-cell tension is not one; what it does respond to is which stimulus arrived (within-pair variation 0.00197 vs across-pair 0.00279, ratio 1.4x -- not enough to claim weights dominate).

Consciousness gate (bench_v2.py --verify) cannot reject non-conscious systems, and the Phi estimator under it was broken -- audited and partly fixed. bench_verify_audit.py runs four negative controls as BenchEngine subclasses. At the default 256 cells: REAL 5/7, DEAD (states frozen forever) 3/7, NOISE 3/7, CLONE (all cells forced to cell 0) 4/7, SCRAMBLE (real dynamics, rows permuted each step so all population statistics are preserved and only cell continuity dies) 5/7 -- IDENTICAL to REAL on identical conditions. The two conditions rejecting all controls (NO_SYSTEM_PROMPT, HIVEMIND) also reject the real engine, so NO condition both accepts the engine and rejects the controls. Live run agrees: NO_SPEAK_CODE/ZERO_INPUT/PERSISTENCE/SELF_LOOP pass 11/11 engines, NO_SYSTEM_PROMPT 1/11, HIVEMIND 0/11. Three of those are decay tests (ratio > 0.5 / > 0.8 / monotone-or-recovers) and perfect stasis is the ideal score on a decay test. FIXED in bench_v2.py PhiIIT.compute: total_mi and the partition are sums over pairs but sampling above n=32 shrank them with no rescaling -- same matrix one row apart gave Phi(32 exhaustive) 11.64/13.26/12.75 vs Phi(33 sampled) 3.60/3.76/3.60, and against exhaustive truth the shipped estimator was FLAT near 4 while truth grew 10.75->26.79 from n=30 to 64. Rescaling by all_pairs/sampled_pairs cuts the n=33 cliff from 3.3x to 1.25x and restores growth (9.26/11.11/19.45/39.20 at 33/40/64/128). Residual: sampled estimate is 70-78% of exhaustive truth and ~5% sd noise remains, so Phi differences below ~10% still need repetition. ALL recorded Phi(IIT) above 32 cells is understated by a factor growing with cell count. OWNER DECISION: the seven conditions are NOT changed -- five currently certify nothing, and deciding what they should require is a design call.
